note: Chrome CPU-throttle proxy for an iPhone XS Max (414x896 @3, mobile profile) on an RTX 3080 Ti host through ANGLE D3D11; the GPU is never the limit there, so CPU-throttled frame times cannot show a texture-bandwidth or fill saving. The texture census (WebGL upload accounting), fetched bytes and renderer memory are the primary measurements of this step; --gpu=swiftshader is a second proxy. No iOS hardware was used. The half pages, the caps and the un-multisampled bakes were implemented on the pre-rebase fable/hmh-perf line (89b9c14c, ea432a70, 11ef0f7f) and cherry-picked onto the rebased steps 3-5 without conflicts as 3820bda2, 55f3786b, 9df58d41.
change: apps/hmh-reboot/src/runtime-performance.mjs: profileTextureUrl() rewrites a runtime page URL (native roster, bagholder roster, production hero pilot, hero motion, held weapons, authored props, Tripo props, terrain tiles/fringes/overlays; .png or .webp, optional query) to <page>@0.5x.webp on the mobile profile only. createProfileTextureLoader(Assets, profile) returns Pixi Assets unchanged on desktop and reduced motion; on mobile it loads the variant and falls back to the full page if the variant fails, so a phone never loses art to a missing half page. main.mjs routes every scalable page through it (pilot atlas, motion page, held-weapon pages, authored props, Tripo props, native roster pages, terrain tiles, fringes and overlays); the mannequin pilot, world design and barriers (which have their own mobile tiers) and the silver coin stay on Assets.load.

@0.5x is Pixi 8's own resolution suffix: loadTextures sets source.resolution = getResolutionOfUrl(url) = 0.5, so the half page keeps the full page's logical size and every frame rectangle, anchor, pivot, trim and UV in the unchanged full-size metadata maps onto it. Nothing changes on-screen size or ground position. tripo-prop-appearance.mjs validates pages against the logical size (source.width) like the hero, motion, held-weapon and roster validators already did.

scripts/build-hmh-mobile-half-res.py writes the 75 variants (48 atlas pages, 11 repeating tiles, 16 U-wrapped strips) reproducibly: premultiplied float32 Lanczos-3 at exactly 2:1, frame-isolated per atlas frame so the 2 px packing gutters cannot bleed, wrap-aware for tiles and strips; lossy WebP q90 with lossless alpha for atlases, lossless exact WebP for terrain. It refuses overlapping half-res frame footprints. --check verifies source freshness, output bytes and per-frame alpha-centroid alignment. The manifest apps/portal/assets/generated/hmh-mobile-half-res.json records source and output SHA-256, bytes and dimensions per page.

Purely visual mobile caps (runtime-performance.mjs profile table): maxAnimatedEnemies 32 -> 24, maxGoreMarks 48 -> 16 (gore-presentation.mjs render({maxMarks}) draws only the newest landed marks, still oldest first; the pool keeps 48 and unlanded marks never use the cap up), resolveAtmosphereBudget halves the mobile fog and mote banks (4+12 -> 2+6), and the contact-shadow, weapon-glow and atmosphere bakes take antialias from the profile so phones skip the multisampled render buffers behind the seven bakes (resolution stays 2; the gradients are unchanged). Desktop (96 / 48 / 10+30 / MSAA) and reduced motion (48 / 48 / 0 / MSAA) are unchanged.

Tooling: scripts/hmh-perf-crowd-bench.mjs --gpu=swiftshader renders WebGL through ANGLE's CPU rasterizer so texture size and fill cost can reach an A/B (absolute times mean nothing there). docs/hmh-reboot/RUNTIME-PERFORMANCE.md profile table gains the blood-mark and texture-page columns.
projectionOnly: No simulation module reads the profile, the loader or a texture. The caps decide only how much art is drawn; the half pages change only which file backs a texture. Evidence: headless digest unchanged, browser census trace digest unchanged and identical on mobile and desktop with full and half pages, determinism/run-summary/evidence suites green.

visual.method: Same-seed crowd census screenshots at tick 1800 (fixed virtual clock, 128-enemy scene) of the full-page and half-page builds, mobile 414x896 @3 (canvas 414x896 at resolution 1) and desktop 1440x900, compared per pixel with .tmp/step6/compare-shots.py: difference statistics, Laplacian-variance sharpness, and the integer shift that best aligns each of nine regions (pivot drift would show as a non-zero shift). Crops at 2x were read by eye.
visual.captures: rebased builds 2026-09-26 (base c34d2a31 full pages vs HEAD half pages, .tmp/step6/bench/census-*); the 2026-09-25 pre-rebase captures (step5 vs step6) give the same per-region numbers and are kept as a cross-check
reading: Every one of the nine regions aligns best at shift [0, 0]: no pivot drift. The hero and every enemy stand at the same size on the same ground line; contact shadows, the target ring and the HUD are unchanged.

Sharpness drops 1.8% over the whole frame and about 9-10% in the actor-dense centre band; terrain (lossless half tiles), HUD and the touch controls are indistinguishable. The difference map is confined to actor edges and the rims of the baked shadow blobs (the un-multisampled bakes).

Actors read slightly softer at the canvas resolution of 1 on a 414 px wide canvas, where a 256 px logical frame is drawn at roughly 50-100 px; the half page still supplies more than one texel per canvas pixel. At the adaptive step-up to 1.5 the margin narrows but stays above one texel per pixel for every roster frame.

Desktop base/head captures differ by at most 3 levels on 0.67% of pixels (sub-visible atmosphere shimmer) with identical sharpness in every region; the pre-rebase pair differed on 50 pixels of 1.3 M. Desktop keeps the full pages.

deferred: Owner-device acceptance on an iPhone XS Max: texture memory pressure, thermal throttling and the WebP decode cost of the half pages are unmeasured on hardware; the host-side gains are memory and bytes, not frame time.
Mipmaps for actor atlases (autoGenerateMipmaps is only on for terrain) and an ASTC/ETC2 compressed path would cut mobile texture memory further; both are separate steps.
The mannequin pilot atlas (pilot-only), the silver coin page and the world-design/barrier pages (which already carry mobile tiers) were left on Assets.load.
Per-archetype lazy roster creation, Pixi 8.19 GCSystem texture release (60 s idle), baked decals and contact shadows were audited and left unchanged (see the 2026-09-25 notes in the doc section).
